standards.name: Chado-XML
standards.abstract: Chado-XML defines an XML representation of the Chado relational database schema so biological data (notably sequence annotation and related modules) can be exported, exchanged, and re-imported. The standard maps Chado tables and columns into XML elements/attributes and supports both a "standard" nested mapping and a more generic mapping via XORT. The specification (GMOD/Chado project) documents syntactic rules, recommended file suffixes, macro-based normalization, and XORT dumpspec attributes; core artifacts (DTD/XSD/RNG/RNC) are referenced for structure validation.

classification.rationale: The source is a schema/mapping specification that enumerates XML elements, attributes and structured constructs (e.g. feature, organism, type_id, dump/test attributes, macro IDs and global accession formats). This is a field-level specification (XML element/attribute names with expected formats/enum choices) rather than prose guidance or an ordered workflow.

standards.name: Chado (relational schema)
standards.abstract: Chado is a modular relational-database schema for representing a wide range of biological research objects — primarily genomic sequences and associated annotations (features such as genes, transcripts, exons), sequence-comparison results, ontologies/controlled vocabularies, phenotypes, genotypes, publications and phylogenies. The recording modality is a relational database (typically PostgreSQL) with tables for features, locations, analyses, controlled vocabularies and many other entities. The standard is published and maintained by the Generic Model Organism Database (GMOD) community (FlyBase contributors and GMOD developers), and addresses the problem of providing a reusable, ontology-driven schema that can represent complex and evolving biological knowledge across organisms. It is modular and extensible (modules for sequence, cv, pub, natural diversity, companalysis, etc.), emphasizes ontology-driven typing (Sequence Ontology, GO, OBO terms) and supplies concrete table definitions and loader/adaptor guidance used by GMOD tools (GBrowse, Apollo, CMap, Tripal).

classification.rationale: The source material includes explicit, named table definitions with column names and SQL types (for example the db, dbxref, cv, cvterm tables and column type information). The documentation supplies concrete table/column schemas (rows/columns) rather than only prose guidance or a sequence-of-steps, so it should be represented as a Metadata Table.
